children: The sharp decline in Brent crude prices and high palm oil inventories are putting pressure on near-term crude palm oil prices, says CIMB Securities analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang in a note. However, inventories are expected to ease in November as production declines from its seasonal peak, potentially supporting prices. Strengthening El Nino conditions could also weigh on output, and potential labor shortages in Malaysia may constrain supply in 2027, she reckons. Ng maintains her 2026 and 2027 CPO price estimates at 4,450 ringgit and 4,550 ringgit a ton, respectively. CIMB has an overweight rating on the plantation sector. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
